traceability.evidence: Core rule implementation and options:,- src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts defines configurable patterns and examples and ties them into the rule: - AnnotationRuleOptions includes: - nested options: story.pattern, story.example, req.pattern, req.example - flat shorthands: storyPathPattern, storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample, autoFix - ResolvedAnnotationOptions contains: storyPattern: RegExp, storyExample: string, reqPattern: RegExp, reqExample: string, autoFix: boolean - Default behavior: - getDefaultStoryPattern(): /^docs\/stories\/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$/ - getDefaultStoryExample(): "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md" - getDefaultReqPattern(): /^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$/ - getDefaultReqExample(): "REQ-EXAMPLE" - Pattern and example resolution: - resolvePattern(...) chooses nested pattern (story.pattern / req.pattern) over flat (storyPathPattern / requirementIdPattern) and falls back to default on missing/invalid values. - resolveExample(...) chooses nested example over flat example over default. - Regex validation and error accumulation: - resolvePattern uses new RegExp(effective.value) and on failure pushes buildInvalidRegexError(...) into optionErrors. - buildInvalidRegexError(field, pattern) -> `Invalid regular expression for option "${field}": "${pattern}"`. - Backward compatibility: - If neither nested nor flat pattern is provided, resolvePattern returns the default hardcoded pattern, preserving existing behavior. - JSON Schema for ESLint options: - getRuleSchema() returns a schema array with an object having properties { story, req, storyPathPattern, storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample, autoFix } and additionalProperties: false, satisfying REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION.,Rule wiring and configuration error reporting:,- src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - meta.messages.invalidRuleConfiguration is defined and explicitly tagged to Story 010.1 and REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION / REQ-BACKWARD-COMP: - "Invalid configuration for valid-annotation-format: {{details}}". - meta.schema is set to getRuleSchema(), so ESLint uses the JSON schema defined above. - create(context): - calls resolveOptions(context.options || []) to produce ResolvedAnnotationOptions and populate optionErrors. - retrieves optionErrors via getOptionErrors(). - Program handler: - If optionErrors.length > 0, iterates and context.report({ node, messageId: "invalidRuleConfiguration", data: { details } }) for each, surfacing regex configuration errors but still continuing to validate comments. - Then iterates all comments and delegates to processComment(context, comment, options).,Use of configurable patterns and examples in validation logic:,- src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-validators.ts: - validateStoryAnnotation(..., options: ResolvedAnnotationOptions): - uses options.storyPattern as the only acceptance check for valid @story values. - when missing, calls buildStoryErrorMessage("missing", null, options) → uses options.storyExample in the message. - when invalid but fixable, uses getFixedStoryPath and options.storyPattern to decide if auto-fix is allowed, and then uses getResolvedDefaults() to ensure backward-compatible behavior on fix. - validateReqAnnotation(..., options: ResolvedAnnotationOptions): - uses options.reqPattern to accept/reject collapsed @req values. - on missing/invalid values, uses buildReqErrorMessage(..., options) → which relies on options.reqExample. - These functions ensure that configured patterns and examples affect validation and error messages as specified in REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG, REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMP, and REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES.,Error message construction with configurable examples:,- src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts: - STORY_EXAMPLE_PATH = "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md" used as default. - buildStoryErrorMessage(kind, value, options): - const example = options.storyExample || STORY_EXAMPLE_PATH; - For kind === "missing": - "Missing story path for @story annotation. Expected a path like \"${example}\"." - For kind === "invalid": - "Invalid story path \"${value ?? ""}\" for @story annotation. Expected a path like \"${example}\"." - buildReqErrorMessage(kind, value, options): - const example = options.reqExample || getDefaultReqExample(); - For kind === "missing": - "Missing requirement ID for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like \"${example}\"." - For kind === "invalid": - "Invalid requirement ID \"${value ?? ""}\" for @req annotation. Expected an identifier like \"${example}\" (uppercase letters, numbers, and dashes only)." - This directly implements REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES using both configurable and default examples.,Tests explicitly tied to Story 010.1 and its requirements:,- tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts header explicitly references the story and requirements: - "Tests for: docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md" - @story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md - Requirement tags: REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK, REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG, REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES, etc. - Valid cases verify configurable patterns: - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY] custom storyPathPattern accepts alternate extension" – uses flat storyPathPattern & storyPathExample. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ] custom requirementIdPattern accepts PROJECT-123 style IDs" – nested req.pattern & example. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH] custom patterns accept alternative story and req shapes" – both nested story/req patterns. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY-FLAT] flat storyPathPattern accepts alternate extension when nested config not provided". - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ-FLAT] flat requirementIdPattern accepts PROJECT-123 style IDs when nested config not provided". - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH-FLAT] flat patterns accept alternative story and req shapes when nested config not provided". - Invalid cases verify examples and fallback behavior: - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES] custom story example appears in error message" – checks that error text uses configured story.example. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-EXAMPLES] custom requirement example appears in error message" – checks that error text uses configured req.example. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid storyPathPattern falls back to default behavior" – options.story.pattern = "[unclosed"; expects: - an invalidRuleConfiguration error with details 'Invalid regular expression for option "story.pattern": "[unclosed"', and - a normal invalidStoryFormat error using the default example, confirming REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION and REQ-BACKWARD-COMP. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK] invalid requirementIdPattern falls back to default behavior" – analogous for req.pattern. - "[REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT] ... storyPathPattern" and "... requirementIdPattern" – analogous for flat shorthand fields. - "[REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG] nested story.pattern takes precedence over flat storyPathPattern and its example" – confirms precedence rules and example usage. - "[REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG] nested req.pattern takes precedence over flat requirementIdPattern and its example". - "[REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES] nested story example text overrides flat storyPathExample in error messages". - "[REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES] nested req example text overrides flat requirementIdExample in error messages". - Jest run output (npm test -- --verbose) shows this suite "Valid Annotation Format Rule (Story 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION)" passing with all the above-named tests green, demonstrating implemented behavior matches the story’s requirements.,Documentation of configurable patterns and examples (user-facing):,- user-docs/api-reference.md, section "traceability/valid-annotation-format" (lines ~80–140): - Documents nested options: - story.pattern – regex source string for @story paths, with default equivalent to ^docs/stories/[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-DEV-[\w-]+\.story\.md$. - story.example – example story path; default "docs/stories/005.0-DEV-EXAMPLE.story.md". - req.pattern – regex source for @req IDs; default equivalent to ^REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+$. - req.example – example requirement ID; default "REQ-EXAMPLE". - Documents flat shorthands explicitly: - storyPathPattern – shorthand for story.pattern; precedence rules defined. - storyPathExample – shorthand for story.example; precedence rules defined. - requirementIdPattern – shorthand for req.pattern; precedence rules defined. - requirementIdExample – shorthand for req.example; precedence rules defined. - Explains behavior notes: - states that patterns must be valid JavaScript regex sources (no surrounding slashes) and that invalid patterns cause a rule configuration error (matching REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION). - states that if options are omitted, the rule behaves exactly as before, relying on built-in defaults (REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT). - This provides clear configuration guidance and examples for the pattern and example options, satisfying the Documentation acceptance criterion for this story.,Interaction with valid-story-reference rule (consistency):,- src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts continues to handle file existence and security using configurable storyDirectories, independent of valid-annotation-format. - Defaults align conceptually: - valid-annotation-format default story regex expects paths under docs/stories/... .story.md. - valid-story-reference uses defaultStoryDirs = ["docs/stories", "stories"]. - user-docs/api-reference.md notes that path format validation (valid-annotation-format) and file existence/boundary checks (valid-story-reference) are complementary, and that valid-annotation-format can be customized for projects that store stories outside docs/stories. - There is no conflicting configuration; pattern checks and storyDirectories operate in separate layers, fulfilling REQ-CONSISTENCY and the Integration acceptance criterion conceptually.
traceability.notes:
The story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md define configurable pattern support for the valid-annotation-format rule, including new options (storyPathPattern, requirementIdPattern and their example counterparts), regex validation with graceful fallback, backward compatibility, and clear documentation.
Implementation in src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts, src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts, and src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-format-validators.ts provides: - Configurable story and requirement patterns via both nested (story.pattern/req.pattern) and flat options (storyPathPattern/requirementIdPattern), - Example strings used in error messages, - JSON-schema-backed option validation, - Regex compilation with explicit configuration error reporting while falling back to default patterns so validation continues.
Tests in tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts are explicitly tagged to this story and cover all key behaviors: custom patterns (nested and flat), example overrides, invalid pattern handling and fallback, and precedence rules. These tests pass in the project’s Jest run, giving strong evidence that the acceptance criteria and listed requirements (REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG, REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION, REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT, REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES, REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION, REQ-PATTERN-TESTING, and consistency with valid-story-reference) are met.
User documentation in user-docs/api-reference.md describes the new options, their defaults, precedence, and usage, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion. Overall, all acceptance criteria for Story 010.1 appear fully implemented and verified by passing tests.
